reason: 2.1.1 ships ':-moz-focusring { outline: none }', which removes Firefox's keyboard focus ring. femto drops that rule (PLAN Conversion rules, vendor prefixes), so in Firefox every keyboard-focused element that sets no outline of its own gets the UA focus ring again: outline-style none becomes auto, and outline-width 3px (the initial medium that 'outline: none' leaves) becomes 1px. In the fixtures that includes the [data-tooltip][tabindex] elements, video and audio[controls]. The selector names only [data-tooltip][tabindex] on components-tooltip.html because the harness focuses only elements that carry data-states, and those are the only such elements it reaches.
notes: Harness hits: in Phase 2's runs (hybrid of forms/basics over its pages and the other pages with tabindex, dialog, iframe, video or audio), Firefox reports only the five span[data-tooltip][tabindex] and the div[data-tooltip][tabindex] of components-tooltip.html in the focus state, 12 records per cell. Beyond the harness, Phase 2's review walked every Tab stop in Firefox at 1280, reference against the basics hybrid: the restored ring also shows on kitchen-sink.html's video, audio[controls] and its span[data-tooltip][tabindex] 'Tooltip on text', which carry no focus state. None of the 150 Tab stops on forms-basics.html differs.

reason: 2.1.1 ships ':-moz-ui-invalid { box-shadow: none }'. Firefox still matches that pseudo-class on a field the user has left invalid (it is the old name of :user-invalid), and at specificity (0,1,0) the rule beat 'input, select, textarea { box-shadow: var(--femto-box-shadow) }' at (0,0,1). So in 2.1.1, Firefox drew no focus ring and no aria-invalid ring on such a field. femto drops the rule (PLAN Conversion rules, vendor prefixes), so Firefox now draws both rings, as Chrome already did with 2.1.1. Safari never matches a -moz- pseudo-class, so it already drew them too.
notes: This entry never hits: no harness state puts a field into :user-invalid, because that takes typing into the field and leaving it. Phase 2's review recorded the difference with a standalone Selenium probe instead: it types into a required email input, a second one with aria-invalid=true and a required textarea, blurs them, then focuses each again. Firefox 160: the reference gives box-shadow none on all three; the basics hybrid gives 'rgb(1, 114, 173) 0px 0px 0px 1.125px' on the email input and the textarea and 'rgb(200, 79, 72) 0px 0px 0px 1.125px' on the aria-invalid one; the hybrid plus only the dropped rule gives none on all three. Chrome draws the rings on both sides, in 157.0.8103.15 and again in 158.0.8127.2 after Chrome Beta updated itself on 2026-10-28.
